Their even perimeters and truncated triangle inequalities imply each lower half-perimeter<=level and each triangle half>=every side. The independent integer enumeration checks all2957 admissible associator entries over levels1..6; the ring formula and callback support are also reviewed against the already admitted ring provider.

Factorial-index invariant: factorials has length level+2 and dimensions length level+1. For any sampled z, all lower<=z<=min(level,upper). Triangle indices half-a,half-b,half-c and half+1 are in range; z+1<=level+1 and each upper-z<=level by the coupled lower-bound/side inequalities, not just by a loose upper<=2*level bound. The13 clean model declarations and the full finite integer enumeration discharge these particular arithmetic conditions. No unchecked private helper accepts arbitrary public index data.

Quantum-number invariant: admit q and its checked inverse t, and require q-t nonzero through difference/difference for[1]. With q*t=1, [2]=q+t and [n+2]=(q+t)[n+1]-[n]. The source loop maintains dimensions[a]=[a+1] and len=a before each later push. The model proves the actual field identity, while vector representation/call-site transport is explicit source reasoning and all six supported levels have direct-root native oracles.

Factorial reuse invariant: start factorials[0]=1; before processing dimension[index], factorials.len()=index+1, so factorials[index] exists. Pushing its product with[a+1] yields the exact prefix factorial[index+1]. For primitive q of order2*(level+2), q-q^-1 and the factors[1]..[level+1] are nonzero in the declared characteristic-zero field; checked scalar refusals still propagate.

Racah invariant: the two fixed arrays enumerate the same lower/upper half-sums as the original coefficient. A max fold from0 and min fold from level are exact for these nonempty nonnegative arrays, eliminating unreachable empty-array errors. The term denominator has four lower and three upper factorials; (-1)^z and the outer half-perimeter sign are kept. Prefactors use dimension[e] and the two original left triangles, preserving the fixed nonorthonormal gauge.

Metric invariant: left/right channel supports and ordering remain unchanged. Each diagonal entry is the inverse of d_channel*d_total times its two squared triangle factors. Actual conjugate-transpose(F)*left*F is compared to right for every stored block before R materialization. This is weighted equality; no positivity or orthonormal-gauge assertion is inferred. The native basis includes raw root factorial/metric oracles, asymmetric sectors, known level2 and Fibonacci gauges and a decisive mismatched-weight refusal.

Phase invariant: root order=8*(level+2) lies in24..64. phase_table starts with1 and each push multiplies the previous power once; it owns exactly one period and never computes a discarded last power. Admitted labels<=6 give each Casimir<=48 and signed exponent in[-96,48]. Euclidean residue is nonnegative and below the positive table length; the natural power at that residue equals the original signed power under the compatible finite-root law. The sign parity is unchanged on admitted fusion channels.

Failure/composition invariant: both early level/field admissions and the metric error priority are retained for lawful scalar inputs. The old per-coefficient signed-power budget could never be exceeded at these exponents; finite-root lookup eliminates that redundant work and its error accumulator. Behavior of non-lawful custom field/root implementations is outside the mathematical contract. Every performed scalar/matrix/category admission remains typed. FusionCategory/BraidedFusionCategory/RibbonFusionCategory private ownership and final validation enforce the actual block, pentagon, both hexagons, dimension, twist and ribbon checks; no partial ribbon value is exposed.

Ownership/cost invariant: coefficient_data computes one q root, one q inverse and one normalization inverse, then O(level) recurrence/factorial work with exact capacities(level+1,level+2). R construction owns one O(level)-size root period and one necessary coefficient clone per R entry; it performs no field exponentiation/inversion inside the coefficient callback. The ring moves once into FusionCategory and later operations borrow category.ring(), avoiding the previous full ring clone. Racah terms stream their seven factors and one running sum without intermediate vectors.

Algorithmic bounds: at rank r=level+1<=7, at most r^4 F blocks and r^2 entries per block are enumerated by the generic provider, each using at most level+1 Racah terms with constant-size factor arrays. Gram products cost cubic work in each actual block dimension and return the two required diagonal matrices. Provider storage/law replay admissions remain the actual DEFAULT_CATEGORY_LIMITS; the final pentagon/hexagon/dimension checks are not represented as merely O(level) construction. Logical scalar counts exclude arbitrary coefficient bit growth, client operation cost, allocation metadata and OS memory.

Final allocation repair: collect only channel-label metadata, then construct each diagonal matrix directly. Row/column indices are bounded by that metadata length, the weight callback runs only on the diagonal, and its owned field value moves directly into final matrix storage. The earlier temporary field-weight buffers are removed.

Allocation review: public q-integer evaluation reuses one q inverse, and the dimension recurrence borrows its retained step at dimensions[1]. Metric diagonals write directly into the required outputs; the category check borrows F-block row/column metadata already owned by that block. The standalone public metric API allocates only its two necessary support lists. Dense Gram products and a complete bounded root period are intentional algorithmic choices, not eliminated operations or minimal-field claims.
